title: Decide the project-local database backend for the port
description:
## Context

zic stored package and file records in datalevin (an embedded Datalog database over H2) inside the .zic-db directory. The store must support packages (name unique, version, location, metadata, dependency refs, file component refs) and files (path unique, size, class normal-file/config-file/ghost-file, SHA-256 checksum), with queries by name, dependers, dependees, file ownership (owned-by?), and (for the orphans story) non-source packages. All writes happen under an exclusive file lock (with-zic-session). Data volume is project-level (tens to hundreds of packages), and the tool's stated goal is "dead simple".

## Decision

Use a file-based store: FSet persistent maps of defstruct records, serialized as a single NRDL document in the .zic-db directory (e.g. .zic-db/packages.nrdl). Reads slurp the store into memory; writes transform the FSet map and atomically replace the file (write temp + rename) while holding the exclusive lock. Datalevin's entity refs become explicit name keys resolved with FSet lookups.

## Alternatives Considered

- (a) SQLite via cl-sqlite/cl-dbi — rejected. Verified 2026-08-12 via swanky: (asdf:load-system "cl-sqlite") fails with "Component cl-sqlite not found" in this ocicl registry. Would also add a C library dependency and a schema/query translation layer, against the "dead simple" requirement.
- (b) FSet + NRDL file store — chosen. All components verified loadable via swanky: (asdf:load-system "fset") and (asdf:load-system "com.djhaskin.nrdl") both return T. Matches dsolv's established data conventions (NRDL cards and index, FSet maps, defstruct records, emit-nrdl-struct methods), no C dependencies, atomic single-file writes, and the existing file lock already serializes writers. Unique package and file identity falls out of FSet map keys.
- (c) Lisp-native prevalence-style store (bknr.datastore, cl-prevalence) — rejected. Not present in ocicl; snapshot/journal machinery adds moving parts with no benefit at project scale.

## Consequences

- .zic-db remains the marking directory located by find-marking-file; the database file lives inside it.
- The port-db bead (zick-q6u) implements slurp-store/save-store (temp + rename), package/file defstructs, and queries as FSet lookups; serialization via nrdl:generate-to with emit-nrdl-struct methods (the dsolv pattern).
- The port-session bead (zick-lky) ensures the exclusive lock covers the read-modify-write cycle of the store file.
- The package record gains an is-source flag naturally, covering the orphans story.
acceptance_criteria: ADR recorded on this bead (Context / Decision / Alternatives Considered / Consequences). Chosen backend components verified loadable via swanky: (asdf:load-system "fset") and (asdf:load-system "com.djhaskin.nrdl") both return T. Rejected alternative cl-sqlite confirmed absent from the ocicl registry.
close_reason: Database backend decided: file-based store with FSet persistent maps serialized as NRDL in .zic-db, mirroring dsolv conventions. Components verified via swanky (fset and com.djhaskin.nrdl load; cl-sqlite not in ocicl).

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text: Verification log 2026-08-12 (swanky, port 4005): fset -> T, com.djhaskin.nrdl -> T, cl-sqlite -> Component cl-sqlite not found. Chose file-based FSet + NRDL store; this unblocks zick-q6u (port-db), zick-lky (port-session), and zick-vqv (scaffold).

title: Port the zic unit tests to Parachute
description: Port test/zic/db_test.clj, test/zic/package_test.clj (linearize: empty, basic, fighter, and cycle cases), and test/zic/session_test.clj to Parachute under tests/, wired into the com.djhaskin.zick/tests ASDF system following the style guide: each test file gets its own subpackage, parachute symbols are named in the defpackage import-from, and the asd test-op performs each package.
acceptance_criteria: (asdf:test-system "com.djhaskin.zick") passes all ported unit tests through swanky.

title: Confirm ocicl availability of the CL libraries the port needs
description:
Map zic's JVM dependencies to Common Lisp and verify each is installable via ocicl before the module ports depend on them.

## Goal

Confirm ocicl availability for: zip handling (zippy), SHA-256 and CRC32 (ironclad), HTTP client (dexador with quri), JSON parsing for package metadata (cl-json or yason), filesystem helpers (cl-fad), file locking (sb-posix flock or equivalent), plus fset, alexandria, cl-ppcre, parachute, and the ported sibling systems com.djhaskin.cliff, com.djhaskin.nrdl, com.djhaskin.svers.

## Findings

All systems verified loadable 2026-08-12 via swanky (port 4005), each (asdf:load-system "X") returning T:

- zippy (zip archives) — OK
- ironclad (SHA-256, CRC32) — OK (first attempt hit a transient swanky EAGAIN; retry succeeded)
- dexador (HTTP client) + quri (URLs) — OK
- cl-json (JSON metadata) — OK; yason also present in ocicl if preferred
- cl-fad (filesystem helpers) — OK
- alexandria, cl-ppcre, parachute — OK
- com.djhaskin.cliff, com.djhaskin.nrdl, com.djhaskin.svers — OK (sibling ports)
- sb-posix — present in SBCL (exclusive file locking via flock for session.lisp)

Decisions recorded:

- Default output format is NRDL, not yaml (user decision 2026-08-12; zic's yaml default is dropped). CLI results print as NRDL documents via nrdl:generate-to / emit-nrdl-struct, mirroring dsolv's main.lisp. cl-yaml is loadable but not needed.
- ocicl.csv / systems.csv were not auto-generated by these loads (every system was already cached in the shared ocicl store). They will appear when a not-yet-cached system is fetched, or when the scaffold bead's com.djhaskin.zick system is first loaded; pin them then.
- If zippy does not expose per-entry CRC values, compute CRC32 by streaming each entry through ironclad's crc32 (noted for the port-fs bead).
- No quickload or qlot usage anywhere; everything resolves through ocicl/asdf.
acceptance_criteria: Final dependency list verified loadable via ocicl/asdf through swanky and recorded in Findings; no quickload/qlot usage; ocicl.csv for zick pinned when the scaffold bead first loads com.djhaskin.zick.
close_reason: All port dependencies verified loadable via swanky (zippy, ironclad, dexador, quri, cl-json, cl-fad, alexandria, cl-ppcre, parachute, fset, cliff, nrdl, svers, sb-posix). Default output format changed to NRDL per user direction.

title: Port zic.package to src/package.lisp (install, remove, verify)
description: Port src/zic/package.clj to src/package.lisp: install-package! (refuse on unmet dependencies, download-package!, package-file-conflicts, config-and-upgrade-precautions with serovers debian-vercmp in-place and downgrade guards and config-fate decisions install/put-aside/do-nothing, unpack with put-aside/exclude/exclude-sum-pool), download-package! (URL filename fallback and staging directory creation), remove-package! (cascade vs refuse, dry-run, linearize via reachable-nodes/sinks, config file backup), remove-without-cascade-internal, verify-package-files!, get-package-info!/get-package-files!/get-package-dependers!/get-package-dependees!. The ported svers provides debian-vercmp.
acceptance_criteria: Parachute tests for linearize covering the empty, basic, fighter, and cycle cases from zic's package_test.clj pass; install and remove flows pass integration tests.

title: Port zic.session to src/session.lisp (database session and file lock)
description: Port src/zic/session.clj to src/session.lisp: with-zic-session (open the database and take an exclusive lock on .zic.lock for the duration of the operation), with-database, path-to-connection-string, and with-filelock raising a descriptive error when the lock is already held. zic used java.nio FileLock with DELETE_ON_CLOSE; use an equivalent OS-level exclusive lock in Common Lisp and remove the lock file on close.
acceptance_criteria: Two concurrent zick sessions cannot both hold the lock; the lock error text matches zic's semantics.

title: Port zic.fs to src/fs.lisp (zip, checksums, download, unpack, marking-file)
description: Port every function in src/zic/fs.clj to src/fs.lisp: archive-contents, archive-entry-checksums, crc-violations, unpack (with put-aside, put-aside-ending, exclude, and exclude-sum-pool options), download (per-host basic/header/oauth-token authorization and insecure flag), stream-sha256, stream-crc, file-sha256, file-size, verify (ghost/config/directory/normal file classes with size and checksum checks), backup-all, remove-files, new-unique-path, all-parents, find-marking-file, list-files. Use zippy for reading zip archives, ironclad for SHA-256 and CRC32, dexador/quri for HTTP, cl-fad for filesystem operations. Keep function-level parity with zic.fs so tests port 1:1. Function names follow CL conventions (no Clojure-style !/? suffixes; -p for predicates).
acceptance_criteria: fs.lisp compiles; unit tests for stream-sha256, stream-crc, and verify! pass; archive fixture tests pass.
notes: Port complete. src/fs.lisp covers all of zic.fs; 13 Parachute tests (60 assertions) green covering checksums, archive checksums/contents, CRC-violation detection (byte-flipped stored zip), unpack paths, verify classes, and path helpers. Port findings: (1) zippy decode-entry callbacks must return the consumed byte count; (2) zippy clobbers crc-32 with the local-header value (0 when a data descriptor is used) during decode-entry, so stored CRCs are captured before computing; (3) SBCL ~x emits uppercase hex, so bytes->hexstr lowercases to match zic; (4) fset:do-seq has no CL-vector method, so iteration over zippy entry vectors uses gmap (:arg :vector) and fset:reduce. All bang/question names dropped per style (backup-all! -> backup-all, remove-files! -> remove-files, file-sha256! -> file-sha256, file-size! -> file-size, verify! -> verify, insecure? -> insecure-p).

title: Port zic.db to src/db.lisp (package and file store)
description: Port src/zic/db.clj to the backend chosen in the decide-db bead: package records (name unique, version, location, metadata, dependencies refs, file component refs), file records (path unique, size, class normal-file/config-file/ghost-file, SHA-256 checksum), init-database!, add-package!, package-id, package-info!/package-info-by-id!, package-files!, owned-by?, package-dependers!/package-dependees!/dependers-by-id!, insert-file!/insert-use!, remove-package!/remove-files!/remove-uses!, clean-for-insert. Follow the porting rules: defstruct for data records, gmap for sequence transforms, FSet for map data, NRDL serialization in place of datalevin's format.
acceptance_criteria: Parachute unit tests mirroring zic's db_test.clj pass against the chosen backend.

title: Port zic.cli to src/main.lisp (CLIFF command line)
description: Port src/zic/cli.clj to src/main.lisp using cliff:execute-program for a program named zick with subcommands add, files, info, init, remove, dependers, dependees, verify; short aliases -k -V -l -m -u -w -W -d -c -C -r -R -n -N -g -G -i -I; defaults (output-format nrdl, start-directory from the current directory, cascade false, dry-run false, download-package true); the setup function that locates the .zic-db marking file via find-marking-file and derives db-connection-string, root-path, staging-path, and lock-path; verify exit codes 3 (package not found) and 4 (verification failures); missing-argument errors per subcommand. Command results print as NRDL documents via nrdl:generate-to / emit-nrdl-struct (dsolv's main.lisp pattern). The list and orphans subcommands stay stubbed (tracked by their own beads). Model the structure on dsolv's main.lisp port.
acceptance_criteria: zick help, init, add, info, files, verify, remove, dependers, and dependees all run against a test database; verify exits 3 or 4 in the right cases; missing package-name errors are raised.

title: Set up zick project scaffolding (ASDF system, ocicl, CLIFF entry point)
description: Follow the djha-skin-common-lisp new-project and cliff-command-line-tool subskills to scaffold com.djhaskin.zick. Create com.djhaskin.zick.asd with the main system and a /tests system, src/ and tests/ directories, ocicl.csv with pinned dependencies, src/main.lisp defining package com.djhaskin.zick with a cliff:execute-program entry point, com.djhaskin.zick.ros via ros init, a Makefile, a README stub, and CHANGELOG.md following keepachangelog. Keep scripts/build and scripts/update-docs that already exist in the repo.
acceptance_criteria: (asdf:test-system "com.djhaskin.zick") runs through swanky with a passing Parachute smoke test; ros build produces the com.djhaskin.zick executable; fmt.ros and lisp-check-parens.ros are clean on all Lisp sources.
close_reason: Scaffolding complete: ASD with main and tests systems, CLIFF entry point, Roswell script, Makefile, changelog, README, gitignore. System loads, tests pass, binary builds and exits correctly.

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text: Completed 2026-08-12. Created com.djhaskin.zick.asd (main + tests systems), src/main.lisp (package com.djhaskin.zick with CLIFF execute-program entry, default-fn, *zick-version*), tests/main.lisp (3 Parachute smoke tests), com.djhaskin.zick.ros, Makefile (build/test/clean), CHANGELOG.md, README.md stub, .gitignore. Validated: (asdf:test-system "com.djhaskin.zick") passes 3/0 via swanky; ./scripts/build produces com.djhaskin.zick; binary exit codes verified (default 0, help 0, unknown subcommand 64); lisp-check-parens.ros clean; fmt.ros clean on src/tests (only the .ros header false-positive shared with dsolv). ocicl pins auto-generate into the shared ocicl.csv via the swank setup.

title: Story: list orphans
description: Complete the TODO.md story: add an is-source notion to the package store (a package installed as a dependency is not a source), graph-sources in package.lisp, non-source-pkgs and used-somewhere? in db, and wire the orphans subcommand in CLIFF (it is commented out in zic.cli). Decide and document what counts as an orphan: installed as a dependency but no longer needed by any remaining package.
acceptance_criteria: Installing a package that depends on b and then removing the depender leaves b reported by zick orphans.

title: Port the black-box test environment (fixture server and zip fixtures)
description: Port the lighttpd-environment test fixture: self-signed certificate, basic auth user mode:code, and wwwroot containing a.zip, b.zip, c.zip, and bad.zip (the bad archive has a corrupted entry for CRC-violation testing). Add black-box shell-script tests in the style of dsolv's test/resources/scripts: test-init, test-add, test-info, test-files, test-verify, test-remove, test-dependers, test-dependees. The CL port does not need the JVM/native-image tracing machinery; provide a script that starts the fixture server and runs the scripts against the built zick binary, asserting exit codes and NRDL output.
acceptance_criteria: All black-box scripts pass against the built zick binary.

title: Expose download authorizations and insecure mode through the CLI
description: zic.fs/download supports per-host basic, header, and oauth-token authorization plus an insecure flag, and zic.package passes (:download-authorizations options) through, but the original CLI never wired a --json-download-authorizations option (it appears only in problems.md test invocations). Add the option to the add subcommand, parse the JSON into per-host authorization records, and confirm the -n/--enable-insecure flag reaches the HTTP client.
acceptance_criteria: zick add with --json-download-authorizations downloads from an auth-protected fixture; insecure mode works against the self-signed fixture.

title: Story: remove package(s) with cascade and dry-run
description: Complete the TODO.md story: zick remove with no dependers removes the package (config files backed up as package.version.backup, normal files deleted, database record removed); with dependers and no --enable-cascade, refuse and list the dependers; with --enable-cascade, linearize and remove dependers first; --enable-dry-run reports the removal set without touching the filesystem; the file lock is held throughout.
acceptance_criteria: All four remove behaviors pass black-box tests; dry-run leaves the project tree untouched.

title: Close the TODO.md test gaps from the install story
description: Per zic TODO.md story 2, cover the listed gaps: (a) test that crc-violations actually catches violations using bad.zip, (b) an instrumented test that download issues the correct HTTP options for basic, header, oauth-token, and insecure, (c) an integration/fs-level test for unpack, (d) a unit test for package serialization/deserialization, and (e) a larger black-box integration test covering install-package! and add! end-to-end on a fresh database: download, unpack, database record, and files on disk.
acceptance_criteria: Every gap in the list has a passing test in the zick suite.

title: Story: install a package next to existing packages
description: Complete the TODO.md story: during install, detect files already owned by other packages (package-file-conflicts and db file-owned?), refuse with a listing of the conflicting files, and provide package-installable? and list-archive-files helpers. Black-box test: installing package b whose archive owns a file already owned by a fails cleanly with the conflict list; installing disjoint packages succeeds and both are queryable.
acceptance_criteria: Conflicting installs are refused with the conflict list; disjoint installs succeed and both packages are queryable.

title: Story: update a package that already exists via install
description: Complete the TODO.md story: pkg-exists?, lookup-pkg-id, erase-pkg, rm-files, list-files, and remove-without-cascade used inside install-package. Verify config-file fate handling (install/put-aside/do-nothing), backup and .new file naming (package.version.backup and package.version.new), downgrade and in-place guards via serovers debian-vercmp, and refusal to reinstall the same version unless allow-inplace is enabled.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrading b 0.1.0 to 0.2.0 over an existing install preserves edited config files (put-aside), removes stale normal files, and updates the database record.

title: Design and implement the list command
description: zic.cli/list! is a FIXME no-op. Decide the scope of zick list (installed packages with name and version, possibly file counts), implement it in CLIFF emitting NRDL output (the default output-format), document it, and cover it with black-box tests. This goes beyond the original code, so record the design decision on the bead.
acceptance_criteria: zick list prints all installed packages with versions; an empty database prints nothing and exits 0.

title: Independent end-to-end audit of the port against zic's intended behavior
description: After the stories land, spin up fresh subagents to audit the port: compare each zic source file to its CL counterpart, replay the TODO.md stories and black-box scripts, run the quality gates (fmt.ros --check, lisp-check-parens.ros, asdf:test-system), and hunt for behavioral drift (exit codes, output format, lock handling, checksum verification, config-file fate). Address every finding. Model this on dsolv's audit beads.
acceptance_criteria: No open audit findings; all quality gates pass; every TODO.md story is black-box passing.

title: Write the scriba manual and publish docs to GitHub Pages
description: Follow the writing-documentation subskill and the pattern established by cliff, svers, and dsolv: docs/scriba/*.scr sections (overview of zick as a zip-based package manager paired with dsolv, getting zick, command reference listing each subcommand's arguments with defaults and aliases, API reference using @cl:doc), docs/manifest.lisp, docs/build-docs.ros with the multi-html TOC link fix, scripts/update-docs, a Makefile docs target, and a .github/workflows/docs.yml modeled on svers, then enable GitHub Pages for the repository. Every referenced function needs a docstring or the build fails.
acceptance_criteria: make docs builds locally; the site publishes at djha-skin.github.io/zick.

title: Release readiness: README, CHANGELOG, Makefile, ocicl publish
description: Fill out README.md with the vision (Zip files In Concert; dead simple; an RPM or DEB for project-level source-code repositories; based almost completely on plain zip files; best paired with dsolv), usage, and examples. Keep CHANGELOG.md per keepachangelog with an entry for each change. Verify ./scripts/build produces the com.djhaskin.zick binary with baked heap and control-stack sizes. Provide Makefile targets for build, test, and docs. Publish zick (and any new dependencies) to ocicl so sibling projects can depend on it.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh clone builds, tests, and runs; the README links the docs; ocicl lists com.djhaskin.zick.
